title: Travel buffer and max-daily-jobs were enforced only in application code; the atomic reservation guard checked raw overlap alone
reproduction: scratchpad repro driving the REAL route twice through a D1 shim that runs the second request at the moment the first request's reservation batch begins - the window two concurrent Workers requests actually share.

measured_before.buffer_sequential_baseline: A 04:00-06:00Z -> 200 groom_arun; B 06:15-08:15Z -> 409 NO_SCHEDULE_AVAILABLE ['Existing booking conflicts with travel/service buffer'].
measured_before.buffer_concurrent: B (interleaved) -> 200 AND A -> 200. Two durable rows 15 minutes apart for a groomer whose configured travel_buffer_minutes is 30.
measured_before.daily_cap_concurrent: groom_arun capped at 2 jobs/day. Three reserves, the third interleaved -> all three 200, three durable rows against a cap of 2.

measured_after.buffer_concurrent: exactly one commits; the loser is answered 409 SLOT_TAKEN and exactly one row is durable.
measured_after.daily_cap_concurrent: two rows durable against the cap of 2; the third is answered 409 SLOT_TAKEN.
measured_after.non_conflicting_control: a 45-minute gap against a 30-minute buffer still commits, sequentially AND when interleaved. Both rows durable.

consequence_closed: Two customers booking at the same moment produced a groomer with jobs 15 minutes apart in different parts of Bangalore, where the platform's own configured travel buffer is 30 minutes - so the second customer would be late or cancelled, and neither customer nor Ops was told. Separately, a provider was committed to more jobs in a day than their own profile caps. Both states were durable, neither surfaced an error, and the only difference between the refused case and the accepted one was request timing.
rule_source: backend/src/scheduling.ts defines the buffer and daily-limit rules as conditions of eligibility; app/api/uat-scheduling/route.ts defined the committing guard as raw overlap alone. The two disagreed. The overnight branch beside it already commits its own rule atomically with SUM(capacity_units)+units<=capacity inside the same INSERT ... SELECT - this is the same treatment for the appointment branch. No product decision is involved.

files_changed: app/api/uat-scheduling/route.ts - the non-overnight INSERT ... SELECT guard now widens the overlap bounds by the provider's own travel_buffer_minutes and adds a same-local-day count against the provider's own max_daily_jobs
backend/src/scheduling.ts - cityOffsetMinutes is exported so the SQL guard keys its daily count on the same local day the engine does
fix.a_repo_control_caught_a_first_draft: The first version restated the city offset inline as `cityIdFor(input)==="blr"?330:0`. tests/city-propagation-closure.test.mjs asserts the scheduling route contains no hardcoded city id and failed on it. The offset is now imported from the engine that owns it - one definition, and the control was right.

sabotage_verification: Buffer widening removed, daily cap intact -> cases 2 and 4 fail, 4 pass.
Daily-cap condition removed, buffer intact -> case 3 fails alone, 5 pass.
non_vacuity_controls: case 1: the sequential baseline still refuses, so the eligibility rule itself is still present and the concurrent case cannot pass for the wrong reason.
case 5: a 45-minute gap against a 30-minute buffer still reserves - the guard must reject conflicts, not second bookings.
case 6: the same non-conflicting booking still commits when interleaved - the guard must reject conflicts, not concurrency.
case 4: the loser is answered 409 SLOT_TAKEN rather than 500 or silence, so the fix cannot be satisfied by dropping a reservation quietly.
